patterns.name: Hardcoded secret or credential in Rust source
patterns.description: A string literal that looks like a credential (JWT secret, API key, password) is assigned directly in source rather than loaded from environment variables or a secret store. This exposes credentials in version control and compiled binaries.
patterns.message: Variable '{target}' in {file} contains what appears to be a hardcoded credential. Load secrets from std::env::var() or a secret manager instead.

patterns.name: Hardcoded fallback when environment variable is missing in Rust
patterns.description: env::var() is called with unwrap_or() or unwrap_or_else() that provides a hardcoded credential when the environment variable is absent. The fallback credential is embedded in the compiled binary.
patterns.message: '{target}' in {file} falls back to a hardcoded value when the environment variable is absent. Remove the fallback — panic or return an Err at startup if the required secret is not configured.
